name: NEC Display
notes: Complete list: 4 actions (src/actions.js) and 3 boolean feedbacks (src/feedbacks.js), registered in one call each; nothing is generated at runtime except the input dropdown choices.

Controls Sharp/NEC displays over TCP (config default port 7142, protocol dropdown 'ascii' or 'hex', default 'hex'; src/config.js). The ASCII protocol sends text commands such as 'power on' terminated by CR, the HEX protocol builds binary packets (src/hexprotocol.js, src/utils.js).

The input dropdown of setInput and the feedback input depends on the protocol chosen in the module config: the lists are built from self.getInputChoices(self.config.protocol) in src/utils.js when the definitions are registered. They are listed in choicesNote, not as closed choices.

HEX protocol inputs (src/hexprotocol.js INPUT_CHOICES): vga, rgbhv, dvi, hdmi1, video1, video2, svideo, tva, tvd, dvdhd1, option, dvdhd2, displayport1, displayport2, hdmi2. ASCII protocol inputs (src/utils.js getInputChoices): hdmi1, hdmi2, hdmi3, displayport1, displayport2, displayport3, mp, compute_module, option. In ASCII mode the id is sent as text ('input <id>') and not checked by the module.

setVolume declares regex: self.REGEX_NUMBER, which is not defined anywhere in the module (it evaluates to undefined), so the field has no effective pattern; the number field also sets range: false. Min 0, max 100.
setPower and setAudioMute 'toggle' work from the module's cached state (self.data.power / self.data.audiomute), not from a fresh device read. The audiomute feedback has no options.
Base library 1.14 (no expression support in options). Variables and presets are not catalogued.

options.label: Input
options.choicesNote: Depends on the protocol set in the module config. HEX: vga, rgbhv, dvi, hdmi1, video1, video2, svideo, tva, tvd, dvdhd1, option, dvdhd2, displayport1, displayport2, hdmi2. ASCII: hdmi1, hdmi2, hdmi3, displayport1, displayport2, displayport3, mp, compute_module, option. The default is the first choice of the active list ('vga' with HEX, 'hdmi1' with ASCII); '' if the protocol is neither.
